messages:
Sam (support): heads-up — AcmeCorp on dedicated pool acme-prod reporting a throughput drop starting ~03:00 UTC. Many requests either 429 throttles or token latency up to ~2.5s/token. Billing alert fired for a sudden token surge. I grabbed a few request IDs and a short log snippet.

Marta (eng-runtime): thanks — can you paste one or two request_ids and any response headers? also include a sample request (size, prompt length).

Sam (support): sure. sample curl we used to repro quickly:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \u002dH 'Authorization: Bearer xxxx' \u002dH 'Content-Type: application/json' \u002d-d '{"model":"rwd-7b-dedicated","input":"summarize...","max_tokens":512}'
```
response headers for req id r-0a1b2c3d: `x-rw-queue-depth: 1184`, `x-rw-batch-size: 1.2`, `x-rw-latency-ms: 2400`, `x-rw-throttle: 1`

Sam (support): small note — customer traffic pattern is many short prompts in parallel from thousands of end users. avg prompt tokens ~48, typical response tokens ~120.

Marta (eng-runtime): those headers point to extreme queue buildup and tiny batches — avg batch size 1.2 is killer for throughput. can we get recent /metrics dump? especially continuous_batcher.queue_depth, max_batch_tokens, prefill_queue_size, scheduler_idle_cycles.

Kai (eng-sre): looking at metrics now — GPU util on acme-prod nodes is low (~22%) but request queue is huge. continuous_batcher shows sustained backlog of ~1.1k, prefill starvation present (prefill_ratio ~0.15). autoscaler logs show no scale-up events after 02:55 UTC — threshold not crossed due to mis-evaluated ready_capacity.

Omar (eng-platform): i see a config flip from last deploy: autoscaler.headroom_pct was reverted to 0.1 in prod canary (should be 0.25). DeployBot triggered at 02:50 UTC: deploy/rollout rwd-autoscale-config v12.

DeployBot: rollout rwd-autoscale-config v12 completed 2026-02-15T02:50:12Z by @omar — changed autoscaler.headroom_pct=0.10.

Marta (eng-runtime): that explains scale inertia, but the immediate throughput hit is from inefficient batching. batcher is sending microbatches because many short requests have high priority flags. check scheduler token_limit and max_batch_tokens — if max_batch_tokens is low we get many tiny batches and high per-token overhead.

Kai (eng-sre): confirmed: max_batch_tokens was set to 256 for acme-prod canary. given response tokens ~120 and many concurrent short requests, effective batch_size collapses. Also continuous_batcher.window_ms is 12 (very tight) — increases context switch overhead.

Marta (eng-runtime): quick mitigations to try (low-risk):
- bump max_batch_tokens -> 1536 for acme-prod
- increase continuous_batcher.window_ms -> 40
- relax prefill_policy to prioritize batching over strict latency SLO for this pool
- temporarily raise autoscaler.headroom_pct -> 0.3 (so we can spin up nodes faster)

Sam (support): i'm on call with customer, will ask them to allow a 5–10% latency tolerance during the mitigation. they agreed to a temporary relaxation.

Omar (eng-platform): i'll roll a canary of those config changes to acme-prod now (autoscaler + batcher). pushing in 2 mins.

DeployBot: canary rollout rwd-batcher-tune initiated by @omar -> target: acme-prod.

Marta (eng-runtime): also check for noisy tenants: any single tenant dominating prefill queue? if so, enable soft-isolation to avoid starving others. run `SELECT tenant_id, count(*) FROM prefill_queue GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 5;`

Kai (eng-sre): ran it — tenant t-acme-chat spikes but it's expected. no one tenant >45% of queue. not strictly noisy-tenant, more global small-batch pattern.

Sam (support): customer reports immediate improvement after ~5m post-change: avg batch-size -> 3.8, queue_depth -> 430, token latency median -> 420ms. still seeing occasional 429s but much fewer.

Marta (eng-runtime): good. next steps:
- Omar: promote config to all acme-prod nodes once canary stable (monitor 15m)
- Kai: investigate why autoscaler.headroom_pct reverted in v12 and add guard in CI
- Marta: write short runbook section for support on "microbatch starvation" mitigation (prefill tuning + headroom)
- Sam: confirm with customer for 24h observation window and keep this thread updated

Sam (support): will do. logging the customer incident and linking this thread to the support ticket. thanks all :thumbsup:

Kai (eng-sre): filing a postmortem checklist item: autoscaler config drift -> assign @omar to root cause follow-up.

Marta (eng-runtime): adding to eng-runtime backlog: investigate adaptive window sizing for continuous_batcher (auto-tune window_ms by arrival rate).

Sam (support): closing the loop with Acme — they want a call tomorrow to discuss long-term options (dedicated capacity sizing vs batching-tuning). scheduling now.

Marta (eng-runtime): nice triage team. keep thread open until 24h stable.

(END)
